topic: Generating Functions and Roots of Unity: The Filter Method
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Computer Science

outline.topic: Generating Functions and Roots of Unity: The Filter Method
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Computer Science

sections.title: Prerequisites: Visualizing Complex Roots
sections.content: Briefly review the n-th roots of unity. Represent ω = e^(i*2π/n) as vectors pointing to the vertices of a regular n-gon on the complex unit circle. Emphasize the 'Filter Property': Σ ω^(jk) = n if n|k, and 0 otherwise.
sections.example: Visual animation: A unit circle showing 4th roots of unity (1, i, -1, -i) spinning and canceling each other out when raised to a power not divisible by 4.

sections.title: From Combinatorics to Polynomials
sections.content: Introduce generating functions as a way to encode sequences. Connect the 'selection' of items to polynomial coefficients. Introduce the persona: 'The Inventory Robot' deciding how many apples and oranges to pack into a crate.
sections.example: Robot packs x types of fruits: (1+x+x^2+...)^k represents choosing any number of fruits for k slots, encoded as the coefficients of P(x).

sections.title: The Roots of Unity Filter (The Core Technique)
sections.content: Explain how to extract the sum of coefficients a_k where k ≡ r (mod n). Show the formula: 1/n * Σ ω^(-rk) * P(ω^k). Use a visual sliding window overlaying the roots of unity onto the polynomial graph.
sections.example: A squirrel collecting acorns: Finding the number of ways to pick a total count of acorns such that the count is a multiple of 3 (n=3) using P(x) = (1+x+x^2+x^3)^N.

sections.title: Synthesis and Application
sections.content: Walk through a step-by-step calculation: defining the polynomial, applying the roots of unity, simplifying the complex powers, and arriving at the final combinatorial result.
sections.example: Final calculation for the squirrel: Using the sum of cubes of binomial coefficients filtered by mod 3 to count configurations where the total is 'balanced' (divisible by 3).

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Visualizing Complex Roots
lecture_lines: Complex roots of unity form a symmetric polygon.
They lie on the unit circle in the plane.
Roots satisfy the sum filter property exactly.
animations: Create a polygon representing complex roots of unity, colored #FFFFFF, positioned relative to [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].
Animate the unit circle, colored #3498DB, appearing with roots on it.
Highlight the sum of roots as zero, using a flashing effect in #E74C3C near [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg].

storyboard.title: From Combinatorics to Polynomials
lecture_lines: Generating functions encode sequences as polynomial coefficients.
The Inventory Robot packs items into distinct slots.
Coefficients count total ways to make selections.
animations: Show a sequence of items, each represented by a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] colored uniquely, e.g., #F1C40F, #2ECC71.
Animate a polynomial expression forming from sequence coefficients, colored #9B59B6.
Highlight the total count as a coefficient in #E67E22 alongside a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] indicating the calculation process.

storyboard.title: The Roots of Unity Filter (The Core Technique)
lecture_lines: Filter coefficients by their indices modulo n.
Apply the roots of unity to extract sums.
The formula sums filtered polynomial values precisely.
Visual window isolates target indices efficiently.
This isolates modulo sum configurations perfectly.
animations: Display indices, color-coded by modulo n, #1ABC9C.
Show root ω applying to polynomial, colored #F39C12.
Display the filter sum formula, using bold #FFFFFF for clarity.
Animate a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/window.svg] frame moving over coefficients in #95A5A6.
Flash the final isolated sum in a bright #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: Synthesis and Application
lecture_lines: Define the target combinatorial polynomial clearly.
Evaluate the polynomial at every root of unity.
Simplify complex power sums to integer results.
Combine values using the inverse filter formula.
Final count emerges from complex arithmetic steps.
animations: Display the combinatorial polynomial, label as 'P(x)' in #3498DB. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg]
Show evaluation points at roots, colored #E74C3C.
Simplify power sums to integers, scaling text to #2ECC71.
Combine terms in the final filter formula, colored #FFFFFF.
